topic: Medicaid Coverage for Pregnant Women in Georgia 2026

title.en: Pregnant in Georgia? Medicaid + Coverage Options 2026
title.es: Embarazada en Georgia: Medicaid y Opciones de Cobertura 2026

description.en: Pregnant in Georgia in 2026? RSM Medicaid covers prenatal care up to 220% FPL with 12 months postpartum. Compare RSM, PeachCare, and Marketplace SEP options.
description.es: Embarazada en Georgia en 2026? El Medicaid RSM cubre atención prenatal hasta el 220% FPL con 12 meses posparto. Compare RSM, PeachCare y opciones del Mercado.

h1.en: Pregnant in Georgia in 2026? Here Are Your Coverage Options
h1.es: Embarazada en Georgia en 2026: Sus Opciones de Cobertura

subhero.en: Georgia's RSM Medicaid covers prenatal care and delivery for incomes up to 220% FPL, with 12 months of postpartum coverage. If you already have Marketplace insurance, a new baby triggers a 60-day Special Enrollment Period to update your plan.
subhero.es: El Medicaid RSM de Georgia cubre atención prenatal y parto para ingresos hasta el 220% FPL, con 12 meses de cobertura posparto. Si ya tiene seguro del Mercado, un nuevo bebé activa un Período de Inscripción Especial de 60 días.

heading.en: Georgia RSM Medicaid accepts applications year-round, no deadline
heading.es: El Medicaid RSM de Georgia acepta solicitudes todo el año, sin fecha límite

body.en: Georgia Right from the Start Medicaid (RSM) is available year-round for eligible pregnant women, no Open Enrollment required. Apply the day you learn you are pregnant. If you have Marketplace coverage and give birth, that birth triggers a separate 60-day Special Enrollment Period to add your newborn or switch plans.
body.es: El Medicaid Right from the Start (RSM) de Georgia está disponible todo el año para mujeres embarazadas elegibles, sin necesidad de Inscripción Abierta. Solicite el mismo día que se entere de su embarazo. Si tiene cobertura del Mercado y da a luz, ese nacimiento activa un Período de Inscripción Especial de 60 días para agregar a su recién nacido o cambiar de plan.

label.en: SEP to add newborn to Marketplace plan (after birth)
label.es: PIS para agregar recién nacido a plan del Mercado (después del parto)

label.en: PeachCare for Kids enrollment (year-round, for children)
label.es: Inscripción en PeachCare for Kids (todo el año, para niños)

quickAnswer.en: Pregnant women in Georgia may qualify for Right from the Start Medicaid (RSM), which covers prenatal care, labor, delivery, and 12 months of postpartum care for incomes up to 220% of the Federal Poverty Level (about $3,967 per month for a household of two in 2026). Georgia has not expanded Medicaid for non-pregnant adults, so eligibility depends on pregnancy status. If you earn above the RSM limit, Georgia Access Marketplace plans with premium tax credits are the next option. Once your baby is born, your newborn qualifies for Medicaid or PeachCare for Kids, and you have a 60-day Special Enrollment Period to update any existing Marketplace plan.
quickAnswer.es: Las mujeres embarazadas en Georgia pueden calificar para el Medicaid Right from the Start (RSM), que cubre atención prenatal, parto y 12 meses de atención posparto para ingresos hasta el 220% del Nivel de Pobreza Federal (aproximadamente $3,967 por mes para un hogar de dos personas en 2026). Georgia no ha expandido Medicaid para adultos no embarazados, por lo que la elegibilidad depende del estado de embarazo. Si gana por encima del límite RSM, los planes del Mercado de Georgia Access con créditos fiscales son la siguiente opción. Una vez que nace su bebé, califica para Medicaid o PeachCare for Kids, y tiene un Período de Inscripción Especial de 60 días para actualizar cualquier plan del Mercado existente.

introParagraphs.en: Georgia's Right from the Start Medicaid (RSM) program is the state's primary coverage pathway for pregnant women. RSM covers all medically necessary prenatal care, labor, delivery, and 12 months of postpartum care, and it accepts applications year-round with no enrollment deadline. Eligibility is based on household income at or below 220% of the Federal Poverty Level, and Georgia counts a pregnant woman as two people in the household size calculation, which effectively raises the income limit. For 2026, that means a single pregnant woman with no other dependents qualifies with income up to about $47,608 per year (treating her as a household of two). Georgia also offers Presumptive Eligibility for RSM, meaning a qualified health center or hospital can issue temporary coverage on the same day you apply, so prenatal visits are covered immediately while the full determination is processed. Georgia is administered by the Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH), and financial eligibility is determined by the Division of Family and Children Services (DFCS). You can apply through the Georgia Gateway portal at gateway.ga.gov, at your local DFCS office, or at a participating Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC). Georgia's postpartum coverage extension to 12 months was approved by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) under the American Rescue Plan Act and has been in effect since 2023, giving Georgia mothers comprehensive care through the critical first year after birth.
introParagraphs.es: El programa Medicaid Right from the Start (RSM) de Georgia es la principal vía de cobertura para mujeres embarazadas en el estado. RSM cubre toda la atención prenatal médicamente necesaria, parto y 12 meses de atención posparto, y acepta solicitudes todo el año sin fecha límite de inscripción. La elegibilidad se basa en ingresos del hogar iguales o inferiores al 220% del Nivel de Pobreza Federal, y Georgia cuenta a una mujer embarazada como dos personas en el cálculo del tamaño del hogar, lo que eleva efectivamente el límite de ingresos. Para 2026, eso significa que una mujer embarazada soltera sin otros dependientes califica con ingresos de hasta aproximadamente $47,608 por año (contándola como hogar de dos personas). Georgia también ofrece Elegibilidad Presuntiva para RSM, lo que significa que un centro de salud calificado puede emitir cobertura temporal el mismo día que solicita, cubriendo visitas prenatales de inmediato mientras se procesa la determinación completa.

introParagraphs.en: Georgia has not expanded Medicaid under the ACA for non-pregnant adults. The state runs a partial expansion program called Georgia Pathways to Coverage requiring 80 hours per month of work or qualifying activity, but pregnant women are EXEMPT from the Pathways work requirement. This means that getting pregnant in Georgia can unlock Medicaid coverage you would not otherwise qualify for as a non-pregnant adult. If your income exceeds the 220% FPL limit for RSM Medicaid, Georgia Access Marketplace plans are the alternative. Georgia Access is the state-based Marketplace (not healthcare.gov), and premium tax credits based on Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) are available for incomes between 100% and 400% FPL for 2026. The ACA subsidy cliff returned for 2026 after enhanced premium tax credits expired January 1, 2026, so incomes above 400% FPL ($63,840 for a single person in 2026) lose access to premium subsidies. Your newborn qualifies for RSM Medicaid from birth, and PeachCare for Kids covers children in households earning up to 247% FPL. Applying for your own coverage and your baby's coverage can happen simultaneously through the Georgia Gateway portal.
introParagraphs.es: Georgia no ha expandido Medicaid bajo la ACA para adultos no embarazados. El estado tiene un programa de expansión parcial llamado Georgia Pathways to Coverage que requiere 80 horas por mes de trabajo o actividad calificada, pero las mujeres embarazadas ESTAN EXENTAS del requisito de trabajo de Pathways. Esto significa que quedar embarazada en Georgia puede abrir cobertura Medicaid que de otra manera no calificaría como adulto no embarazado. Si sus ingresos superan el límite del 220% FPL para el Medicaid RSM, los planes del Mercado de Georgia Access son la alternativa. Georgia Access es el Mercado basado en el estado, y los créditos fiscales de prima basados en el Ingreso Bruto Ajustado Modificado (MAGI) están disponibles para ingresos entre el 100% y el 400% FPL para 2026.

name.en: Apply for Right from the Start Medicaid (RSM) immediately
name.es: Solicite el Medicaid Right from the Start (RSM) de inmediato

text.en: Apply as soon as you confirm your pregnancy at gateway.ga.gov, your local DFCS office, or a participating FQHC. Georgia's Presumptive Eligibility allows a qualified health center to approve temporary RSM coverage the same day, so prenatal visits are covered immediately. Do not wait for a formal determination to start care.
text.es: Solicite tan pronto como confirme su embarazo en gateway.ga.gov, su oficina local de DFCS, o un FQHC participante. La Elegibilidad Presuntiva de Georgia permite que un centro de salud calificado apruebe cobertura RSM temporal el mismo día, para que las visitas prenatales se cubran de inmediato.

name.en: Calculate your household income against the 220% FPL limit
name.es: Calcule su ingreso del hogar contra el límite del 220% FPL

text.en: Georgia RSM counts you as two people (you and your unborn baby). For 2026, 220% FPL for a household of two is approximately $47,608 per year or $3,967 per month. Add any additional household members to increase your limit. Use gross income before taxes. If income is above 220% FPL, compare Georgia Access Marketplace plans with premium tax credits instead.
text.es: El RSM de Georgia lo cuenta como dos personas (usted y su bebé por nacer). Para 2026, el 220% FPL para un hogar de dos personas es aproximadamente $47,608 por año o $3,967 por mes. Agregue miembros adicionales del hogar para aumentar su límite. Use ingreso bruto antes de impuestos. Si el ingreso es superior al 220% FPL, compare los planes del Mercado de Georgia Access con créditos fiscales de prima.

name.en: Gather your documents before submitting the Georgia Gateway application
name.es: Reuna sus documentos antes de enviar la solicitud de Georgia Gateway

text.en: Submit your application through the Georgia Gateway portal at gateway.ga.gov with proof of pregnancy (letter or document from your doctor or midwife), proof of Georgia residency (utility bill, lease, or driver's license), proof of income (recent pay stubs, self-employment records, or unemployment award letter), Social Security number, and your doctor's name and contact information. Missing documents are the leading cause of RSM application delays.
text.es: Envíe su solicitud a través del portal Georgia Gateway en gateway.ga.gov con prueba de embarazo (carta o documento de su médico o partera), prueba de residencia en Georgia (factura de servicios, contrato de arrendamiento o licencia de conducir), prueba de ingresos (talones de pago recientes, registros de trabajo por cuenta propia o carta de desempleo), número de Seguro Social e información de contacto de su médico.

name.en: If income exceeds 220% FPL, enroll through Georgia Access Marketplace
name.es: Si los ingresos superan el 220% FPL, inscríbase a través del Mercado de Georgia Access

text.en: Log in to georgiaaccess.gov and compare ACA Marketplace plans during Open Enrollment (November 1, 2026 through January 15, 2027 for 2027 coverage). Pregnancy does not trigger a Special Enrollment Period in Georgia Access, but birth does. Marketplace plans cover maternity care as an essential health benefit. Premium tax credits are available for incomes between 100% and 400% FPL in 2026, reducing monthly premiums significantly.
text.es: Inicie sesión en georgiaaccess.gov y compare planes del Mercado ACA durante la Inscripción Abierta (del 1 de noviembre de 2026 al 15 de enero de 2027 para cobertura 2027). El embarazo no activa un Período de Inscripción Especial en Georgia Access, pero el parto sí. Los planes del Mercado cubren atención de maternidad como beneficio esencial de salud.

name.en: Enroll your newborn in Medicaid or PeachCare for Kids within 60 days of birth
name.es: Inscriба a su recién nacido en Medicaid o PeachCare for Kids dentro de los 60 días del nacimiento

text.en: Your newborn qualifies for RSM Medicaid from birth if your household income is within Medicaid limits, or PeachCare for Kids (Georgia's CHIP program) for incomes up to 247% FPL. Apply at gateway.ga.gov within 60 days of birth. If you have a Marketplace plan, birth triggers a 60-day Special Enrollment Period to add your baby to your existing plan or switch to a new plan starting the date of birth.
text.es: Su recién nacido califica para el Medicaid RSM desde el nacimiento si el ingreso de su hogar está dentro de los límites de Medicaid, o para PeachCare for Kids (programa CHIP de Georgia) para ingresos hasta el 247% FPL. Solicite en gateway.ga.gov dentro de los 60 días del nacimiento. Si tiene un plan del Mercado, el nacimiento activa un Período de Inscripción Especial de 60 días para agregar a su bebé.

name.en: Confirm your 12-month postpartum RSM coverage stays active
name.es: Confirme que su cobertura RSM posparto de 12 meses permanece activa

text.en: Georgia's RSM postpartum coverage automatically extends 12 months after birth for mothers enrolled during pregnancy. You do not need to reapply or requalify for this extension. However, watch for a Medicaid renewal notice around month 12 and complete it on time at gateway.ga.gov to avoid a coverage gap. Keep your address current in the Georgia Gateway portal so renewal notices reach you.
text.es: La cobertura posparto RSM de Georgia se extiende automáticamente 12 meses después del parto para madres inscritas durante el embarazo. No necesita volver a solicitar ni recalificar para esta extensión. Sin embargo, esté atenta a un aviso de renovación de Medicaid alrededor del mes 12 y complételo a tiempo en gateway.ga.gov para evitar una brecha de cobertura.

name.en: After RSM ends, check eligibility for Georgia Pathways or Marketplace
name.es: Después del RSM, verifique elegibilidad para Georgia Pathways o el Mercado

text.en: When your 12-month postpartum RSM coverage ends, check whether you qualify for Georgia Pathways to Coverage (partial Medicaid expansion for adults who meet 80 hours per month work requirements and income under 100% FPL) or for ACA Marketplace plans. The end of postpartum Medicaid is a qualifying life event triggering a 60-day Special Enrollment Period for Marketplace enrollment at georgiaaccess.gov.
text.es: Cuando finalice su cobertura RSM posparto de 12 meses, verifique si califica para Georgia Pathways to Coverage (expansión parcial de Medicaid para adultos que cumplen 80 horas por mes de requisitos de trabajo e ingresos bajo el 100% FPL) o para planes del Mercado ACA. El fin del Medicaid posparto es un evento calificador que activa un Período de Inscripción Especial de 60 días.

intro.en: The most common mistakes pregnant women in Georgia make when seeking coverage in 2026:
intro.es: Los errores mas comunes que cometen las mujeres embarazadas en Georgia al buscar cobertura en 2026:

items.en: Waiting to apply for RSM Medicaid until late in pregnancy. Apply as soon as you confirm pregnancy. Georgia's Presumptive Eligibility means you can get same-day temporary coverage at a participating health center for your first prenatal visit.
items.es: Esperar a solicitar el Medicaid RSM hasta tarde en el embarazo. Solicite tan pronto como confirme el embarazo. La Elegibilidad Presuntiva de Georgia permite cobertura temporal el mismo dia en un centro de salud participante para su primera visita prenatal.

items.en: Forgetting that Georgia counts you as two people. A pregnant woman is counted as a household of two (or more, if she has other children). This means your income limit for RSM is higher than you might expect based on looking up the 220% FPL for a household of one.
items.es: Olvidar que Georgia la cuenta como dos personas. Una mujer embarazada se cuenta como un hogar de dos (o mas, si tiene otros hijos). Esto significa que su limite de ingresos para RSM es mas alto de lo que podria esperar si busca el 220% FPL para un hogar de uno.

items.en: Assuming pregnancy triggers a Marketplace Special Enrollment Period. In Georgia, pregnancy alone does NOT trigger an SEP on Georgia Access. Birth does. If you are uninsured and pregnant and earn above RSM limits, you may have to wait for Open Enrollment unless another qualifying event applies.
items.es: Asumir que el embarazo activa un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial del Mercado. En Georgia, el embarazo solo NO activa un PIS en Georgia Access. El parto si lo hace. Si no tiene seguro y esta embarazada y gana por encima de los limites del RSM, puede tener que esperar la Inscripcion Abierta.

items.en: Not enrolling the newborn immediately after birth. Your baby qualifies for RSM Medicaid or PeachCare for Kids from the date of birth. Apply within 60 days at gateway.ga.gov. Missing this window means your baby has no coverage until the next Open Enrollment.
items.es: No inscribir al recien nacido inmediatamente despues del parto. Su bebe califica para el Medicaid RSM o PeachCare for Kids desde la fecha de nacimiento. Solicite dentro de los 60 dias en gateway.ga.gov.

items.en: Missing the 12-month postpartum Medicaid renewal notice. Georgia RSM postpartum coverage lasts 12 months but requires renewal after that. Watch for a renewal letter around month 11 and respond promptly. An outdated address in Georgia Gateway is the leading reason women lose postpartum coverage unnecessarily.
items.es: No responder al aviso de renovacion del Medicaid posparto de 12 meses. La cobertura posparto RSM de Georgia dura 12 meses pero requiere renovacion despues. Este atenta a una carta de renovacion alrededor del mes 11 y responda con prontitud.

items.en: Defaulting to COBRA without comparing to RSM Medicaid. If you were on employer coverage before becoming pregnant, COBRA costs 102% of the full premium, typically $400 to $2,000 per month. RSM Medicaid is free if your income qualifies. Check RSM eligibility before electing COBRA.
items.es: Elegir COBRA automaticamente sin comparar con el Medicaid RSM. Si tenia cobertura del empleador antes de quedar embarazada, COBRA cuesta el 102% de la prima completa, tipicamente $400 a $2,000 por mes. El Medicaid RSM es gratuito si sus ingresos califican.

heading.en: Georgia RSM Medicaid: What It Covers and Who Qualifies in 2026
heading.es: Medicaid RSM de Georgia: Que Cubre y Quien Califica en 2026

paragraphs.en: Georgia Right from the Start Medicaid (RSM) is administered by the Georgia Department of Community Health (DCH) and is the state's core prenatal coverage program. RSM covers all medically necessary prenatal care, laboratory tests, ultrasounds, prescription drugs, mental health services related to pregnancy, labor, and delivery, and 12 months of postpartum care for the mother. Coverage begins from the date of application approval or the date of Presumptive Eligibility, which can be the same day you walk into a participating Federally Qualified Health Center or county health department. Georgia extended postpartum RSM coverage to 12 months in 2023 under the American Rescue Plan Act, a significant expansion from the previous 60-day postpartum period. This 12-month extension is automatic; no reapplication is needed after birth, though a Medicaid renewal is required at the 12-month mark. Income eligibility for RSM is set at 220% of the Federal Poverty Level, and Georgia's rules treat a pregnant woman as a household of at least two people, meaning the effective income limit for a single pregnant woman in 2026 is approximately $47,608 per year (220% of the $21,640 two-person FPL guideline) rather than the lower one-person threshold.
paragraphs.es: El Medicaid Right from the Start (RSM) de Georgia es administrado por el Departamento de Salud Comunitaria de Georgia (DCH) y es el programa central de cobertura prenatal del estado. RSM cubre toda la atención prenatal médicamente necesaria, pruebas de laboratorio, ultrasonidos, medicamentos recetados, servicios de salud mental relacionados con el embarazo, parto y 12 meses de atención posparto para la madre. La cobertura comienza desde la fecha de aprobacion de la solicitud o la fecha de Elegibilidad Presuntiva. Georgia extendio la cobertura posparto RSM a 12 meses en 2023 bajo la Ley del Plan de Rescate Americano, una expansion significativa del periodo posparto previo de 60 dias.

paragraphs.en: Managed care organizations (MCOs) deliver RSM benefits in Georgia. The contracted plans for 2026 include Amerigroup Georgia, Peach State Health Management (a Centene company), and WellCare of Georgia. Once approved for RSM, Georgia will assign you to a managed care plan or you can choose one. Each MCO maintains its own provider network, so confirm your OB/GYN and preferred hospital are in-network with your assigned plan immediately after enrollment. Provider network differences among Georgia MCOs are a common source of confusion for newly enrolled pregnant women. Switching MCOs is permitted within 90 days of initial enrollment if you are dissatisfied with your assigned plan.
paragraphs.es: Las organizaciones de atencion administrada (MCO) brindan los beneficios RSM en Georgia. Los planes contratados para 2026 incluyen Amerigroup Georgia, Peach State Health Management y WellCare de Georgia. Una vez aprobada para RSM, Georgia le asignara un plan de atencion administrada o podra elegir uno. Cada MCO mantiene su propia red de proveedores, por lo que confirme que su obstetra y hospital preferido esten en la red con su plan asignado inmediatamente despues de la inscripcion.

heading.en: Georgia Coverage Gap: What to Do If You Earn Too Much for RSM but Cannot Afford Marketplace
heading.es: Brecha de Cobertura en Georgia: Que Hacer Si Gana Demasiado para RSM pero No Puede Pagar el Mercado

paragraphs.en: Georgia has not expanded Medicaid under the ACA for non-pregnant adults. This creates a coverage gap: adults earning under 100% FPL ($15,960 per year for a single person in 2026) who are not pregnant and do not meet Georgia Pathways work requirements cannot get Medicaid AND cannot get ACA Marketplace subsidies (which start at 100% FPL). For pregnant women, the RSM program reaches up to 220% FPL, so most pregnant women clear the gap. However, after your postpartum RSM ends at 12 months, you may fall back into the gap if your income is under 100% FPL. Three options at that point: Georgia Pathways to Coverage (income under 100% FPL, must meet 80 hours per month work or qualifying activity, per the program's CMS-approved waiver through December 2026); Family Medicaid for parents with children under 19 whose income meets legacy income rules (typically very low); or self-pay at a Federally Qualified Health Center, which uses sliding-scale fees based on income.
paragraphs.es: Georgia no ha expandido Medicaid bajo la ACA para adultos no embarazados. Esto crea una brecha de cobertura: adultos que ganan menos del 100% FPL ($15,960 al ano para una sola persona en 2026) que no estan embarazadas y no cumplen los requisitos de trabajo de Georgia Pathways no pueden obtener Medicaid NI subsidios del Mercado ACA. Para las mujeres embarazadas, el programa RSM llega hasta el 220% FPL, por lo que la mayoria de las mujeres embarazadas superan la brecha.

paragraphs.en: Georgia Access Marketplace plans cover maternity care as a federally mandated essential health benefit, so any plan you select through georgiaaccess.gov will include prenatal visits, delivery, and newborn care. For incomes between 100% and 400% FPL in 2026, premium tax credits reduce monthly premiums significantly. The 2026 ACA subsidy cliff returned after enhanced premium tax credits from the Inflation Reduction Act expired January 1, 2026, so incomes above 400% FPL ($63,840 for a single person in 2026) no longer receive premium subsidies. If your income is between 220% FPL (RSM limit) and 400% FPL, a Silver plan with cost-sharing reductions or a Bronze plan are typically the most affordable Marketplace options in Georgia in 2026. Use the Georgia Access subsidy calculator at georgiaaccess.gov to compare plans by your specific income and household size.
paragraphs.es: Los planes del Mercado de Georgia Access cubren la atencion de maternidad como beneficio esencial de salud obligatorio por ley federal, por lo que cualquier plan que seleccione a traves de georgiaaccess.gov incluira visitas prenatales, parto y atencion al recien nacido. Para ingresos entre el 100% y el 400% FPL en 2026, los creditos fiscales de prima reducen significativamente las primas mensuales. El umbral de subsidio ACA de 2026 regreso despues de que los creditos fiscales de prima mejorados expiraron el 1 de enero de 2026.

heading.en: PeachCare for Kids: Georgia CHIP Coverage for Your Newborn in 2026
heading.es: PeachCare for Kids: Cobertura CHIP de Georgia para Su Recien Nacido en 2026

paragraphs.en: PeachCare for Kids is Georgia's Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), providing comprehensive coverage for children from birth through age 18 in households that earn too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private insurance. For 2026, PeachCare for Kids covers children in households earning between 138% and 247% of the Federal Poverty Level. Children under 138% FPL qualify for full Medicaid. PeachCare for Kids covers well-child visits, immunizations, vision, dental, prescription drugs, mental health services, and emergency care, with premiums as low as $0 to $35 per month depending on household income. Enrollment is year-round through the Georgia Gateway portal at gateway.ga.gov. Your newborn qualifies from the date of birth, and applying within 60 days of birth ensures no coverage gap. PeachCare for Kids is administered by the same MCOs as Medicaid in Georgia, so the same Amerigroup, Peach State, and WellCare networks apply.
paragraphs.es: PeachCare for Kids es el Programa de Seguro Medico para Ninos (CHIP) de Georgia, que brinda cobertura integral para ninos desde el nacimiento hasta los 18 anos en hogares que ganan demasiado para Medicaid pero no pueden pagar seguro privado. Para 2026, PeachCare for Kids cubre ninos en hogares que ganan entre el 138% y el 247% del Nivel de Pobreza Federal. Los ninos bajo el 138% FPL califican para Medicaid completo. PeachCare for Kids cubre visitas de bienestar infantil, vacunas, vision, dental, medicamentos recetados, servicios de salud mental y atencion de emergencia, con primas tan bajas como $0 a $35 por mes segun el ingreso del hogar.

heading.en: COBRA vs. Georgia RSM Medicaid: Which Is Right for You?
heading.es: COBRA vs. Medicaid RSM de Georgia: Cual Es la Mejor Opcion para Usted?

paragraphs.en: Pregnant women who recently lost employer-based health coverage face a specific comparison: COBRA continuation of the former employer's plan versus Georgia RSM Medicaid. COBRA preserves your old plan at 102% of the full premium cost, typically $400 to $900 per month for an individual and $1,200 to $2,800 per month for family coverage in 2026. RSM Medicaid is free with no premiums and no copays for covered prenatal and delivery services. The decision framework is straightforward: check RSM eligibility first. If your current income (counting yourself as two) is at or below 220% FPL, RSM Medicaid is the better choice for your prenatal care because it costs nothing. COBRA only makes sense if your income is above 220% FPL AND you need to maintain a specific OB/GYN who is not in any Georgia Marketplace network, OR if you have an existing complex pregnancy that requires continuity with a high-risk specialist whose practice is not contracted with any Georgia Medicaid MCO. The COBRA election window is 60 days from the qualifying event that caused coverage loss. Do not let the COBRA election window expire while you decide; you can elect COBRA and then drop it later if RSM is approved, but you cannot elect COBRA after the 60-day window closes.
paragraphs.es: Las mujeres embarazadas que recientemente perdieron cobertura de salud del empleador enfrentan una comparacion especifica: la continuacion COBRA del plan del empleador anterior versus el Medicaid RSM de Georgia. COBRA mantiene su plan anterior al 102% del costo total de la prima, tipicamente $400 a $900 por mes para un individuo y $1,200 a $2,800 por mes para cobertura familiar en 2026. El Medicaid RSM es gratuito sin primas ni copagos para servicios prenatales y de parto cubiertos. El marco de decision es directo: verifique la elegibilidad RSM primero. Si su ingreso actual (contandose como dos) es igual o inferior al 220% FPL, el Medicaid RSM es la mejor opcion para su atencion prenatal.

en.question: What is the income limit for Georgia Medicaid while pregnant in 2026?
en.answer: Georgia Right from the Start Medicaid (RSM) covers pregnant women with household income at or below 220% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL). Georgia counts a pregnant woman as two household members, so the effective 2026 income limit for a single pregnant woman with no other dependents is approximately $47,608 per year or $3,967 per month. This is based on the 2026 FPL guideline for a household of two ($21,640), multiplied by 220%. Each additional household member adds roughly $12,496 per year to the income limit. Apply at gateway.ga.gov or your local DFCS office; there is no income asset test for RSM.

en.question: Does pregnancy trigger a Special Enrollment Period in Georgia?
en.answer: No. In Georgia, pregnancy alone does not trigger a Special Enrollment Period (SEP) on the Georgia Access Marketplace. Birth does trigger a 60-day SEP, allowing you to add your newborn to an existing Marketplace plan or enroll in a new Marketplace plan with coverage retroactive to the date of birth. If you are uninsured, pregnant, and earn above RSM income limits, your best option is to apply for RSM Medicaid (which is year-round, no SEP needed) or wait for the next Open Enrollment period at georgiaaccess.gov. Some states running their own state-based Marketplaces do allow pregnancy as an SEP trigger, but Georgia Access does not as of 2026.

en.question: How long does Georgia Medicaid cover me after I give birth?
en.answer: Georgia extends RSM Medicaid postpartum coverage for 12 months after birth for mothers who were enrolled in RSM during pregnancy. This extension was approved by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) under the American Rescue Plan Act and took effect in Georgia in 2023. You do not need to reapply or requalify for the postpartum extension; it is automatic. However, a Medicaid eligibility renewal is required at the end of the 12 months. Watch for a renewal notice from DFCS around month 11, respond promptly, and keep your address current in the Georgia Gateway portal to ensure renewal paperwork reaches you.

en.question: What if I cannot afford COBRA and I do not qualify for RSM Medicaid?
en.answer: If your income is above 220% FPL (disqualifying you from RSM) and you recently lost employer coverage, three pathways remain. First, apply for a Georgia Access Marketplace plan during a Special Enrollment Period triggered by your coverage loss (60 days from the loss date), which is separate from the pregnancy-related SEP. Premium tax credits are available for incomes between 100% and 400% FPL in 2026 at georgiaaccess.gov. Second, if your income dropped significantly, you may now qualify for RSM or Georgia Pathways to Coverage, check again. Third, seek care at a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) using sliding-scale fees while you arrange coverage; FQHCs are required to see patients regardless of ability to pay.

en.question: Does my newborn automatically get Georgia Medicaid?
en.answer: Not automatically, but the process is straightforward. If you are enrolled in RSM Medicaid when your baby is born, your newborn qualifies for Medicaid from the date of birth. You must still apply for your baby separately through the Georgia Gateway portal at gateway.ga.gov within 60 days of birth to establish their individual Medicaid record. Babies born to RSM-enrolled mothers typically receive Medicaid without income requalification for the first year. If your household income is above Medicaid limits but under 247% FPL, apply for PeachCare for Kids instead. Apply within 60 days of birth to avoid a coverage gap.

en.question: Can undocumented immigrants get RSM Medicaid for pregnancy in Georgia?
en.answer: Federal law (Emergency Medicaid, 42 CFR 440.255) requires states to cover emergency labor and delivery services for undocumented immigrants regardless of immigration status. Georgia provides Emergency Medicaid for this purpose, covering labor, delivery, and treatment of emergency medical conditions. Emergency Medicaid does not cover prenatal care in Georgia; it is limited to the emergency delivery event itself. Undocumented immigrants who are pregnant and seeking prenatal care should contact a Federally Qualified Health Center, which provides sliding-scale prenatal care regardless of immigration status. Some counties also offer county health department prenatal services.

en.question: What documents do I need to apply for RSM Medicaid while pregnant in Georgia?
en.answer: Georgia RSM Medicaid requires proof of pregnancy (a signed letter from your doctor or midwife), proof of Georgia residency (utility bill, lease, or driver's license showing a physical Georgia address), proof of income (recent pay stubs, unemployment award letter, or self-employment income records), Social Security numbers for all household members, and proof of citizenship or qualifying immigration status. You can apply online at gateway.ga.gov, at your local DFCS office, or at a participating health center for Presumptive Eligibility, which provides same-day temporary coverage while the full application is processed.

en.question: After my postpartum RSM ends, what are my options in Georgia?
en.answer: When your 12-month postpartum RSM coverage ends, you have several options. Loss of Medicaid is a qualifying life event that triggers a 60-day Special Enrollment Period for the Georgia Access Marketplace; enroll at georgiaaccess.gov within 60 days for an ACA Marketplace plan with premium tax credits if your income is between 100% and 400% FPL in 2026. If your income is under 100% FPL, apply for Georgia Pathways to Coverage (partial Medicaid expansion requiring 80 hours per month work activity) or Family Medicaid if you have children under 19. If you become pregnant again, RSM eligibility restarts immediately.

es.question: Cual es el limite de ingresos para el Medicaid de Georgia durante el embarazo en 2026?
es.answer: El Medicaid Right from the Start (RSM) de Georgia cubre a mujeres embarazadas con ingresos del hogar iguales o inferiores al 220% del Nivel de Pobreza Federal (FPL). Georgia cuenta a una mujer embarazada como dos miembros del hogar, por lo que el limite de ingresos de 2026 para una mujer embarazada soltera sin otros dependientes es aproximadamente $47,608 al ano o $3,967 al mes. Cada miembro adicional del hogar agrega aproximadamente $12,496 al ano al limite de ingresos. Solicite en gateway.ga.gov o en su oficina local de DFCS; no hay prueba de activos para RSM.

es.question: El embarazo activa un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial en Georgia?
es.answer: No. En Georgia, el embarazo solo no activa un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (PIS) en el Mercado de Georgia Access. El parto si activa un PIS de 60 dias, lo que le permite agregar a su recien nacido a un plan del Mercado existente o inscribirse en un nuevo plan con cobertura retroactiva a la fecha de nacimiento. Si no tiene seguro, esta embarazada y gana por encima de los limites de ingresos del RSM, su mejor opcion es solicitar el Medicaid RSM (que es todo el ano, no necesita PIS) o esperar el siguiente periodo de Inscripcion Abierta en georgiaaccess.gov.

es.question: Durante cuanto tiempo me cubre el Medicaid de Georgia despues de dar a luz?
es.answer: Georgia extiende la cobertura posparto del Medicaid RSM por 12 meses despues del parto para madres inscritas en RSM durante el embarazo. Esta extension fue aprobada por los Centros de Servicios de Medicare y Medicaid (CMS) bajo la Ley del Plan de Rescate Americano y entro en vigor en Georgia en 2023. No necesita volver a solicitar ni recalificar para la extension posparto; es automatica. Sin embargo, se requiere una renovacion de elegibilidad de Medicaid al final de los 12 meses.

es.question: Que pasa si no puedo pagar COBRA y no califico para el Medicaid RSM?
es.answer: Si sus ingresos estan por encima del 220% FPL y perdio recientemente la cobertura del empleador, quedan tres opciones. Primero, solicite un plan del Mercado de Georgia Access durante un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial activado por la perdida de cobertura (60 dias desde la fecha de perdida). Los creditos fiscales de prima estan disponibles para ingresos entre el 100% y el 400% FPL en 2026 en georgiaaccess.gov. Segundo, si sus ingresos bajaron significativamente, puede que ahora califique para RSM. Tercero, busque atencion en un Centro de Salud Calificado Federalmente usando honorarios de escala deslizante.

es.question: Mi recien nacido recibe automaticamente el Medicaid de Georgia?
es.answer: No automaticamente, pero el proceso es sencillo. Si esta inscrita en el Medicaid RSM cuando nace su bebe, su recien nacido califica para Medicaid desde la fecha de nacimiento. Aun debe solicitar para su bebe por separado a traves del portal Georgia Gateway en gateway.ga.gov dentro de los 60 dias del nacimiento. Si el ingreso de su hogar esta por encima de los limites de Medicaid pero por debajo del 247% FPL, solicite PeachCare for Kids.

es.question: Pueden los inmigrantes indocumentados obtener Medicaid RSM por embarazo en Georgia?
es.answer: La ley federal (Medicaid de Emergencia, 42 CFR 440.255) requiere que los estados cubran servicios de parto de emergencia para inmigrantes indocumentados independientemente del estatus migratorio. Georgia proporciona Medicaid de Emergencia para este proposito, cubriendo el parto y el tratamiento de condiciones medicas de emergencia. El Medicaid de Emergencia no cubre la atencion prenatal en Georgia. Las inmigrantes indocumentadas que buscan atencion prenatal deben contactar un Centro de Salud Calificado Federalmente, que brinda atencion prenatal de escala deslizante independientemente del estatus migratorio.

es.question: Que documentos necesito para solicitar el Medicaid RSM embarazada en Georgia?
es.answer: El Medicaid RSM de Georgia requiere prueba de embarazo (carta firmada de su medico o partera), prueba de residencia en Georgia (factura de servicios, contrato de arrendamiento o licencia de conducir con direccion fisica en Georgia), prueba de ingresos (talones de pago recientes, carta de desempleo o registros de ingresos por cuenta propia), numeros de Seguro Social para todos los miembros del hogar, y prueba de ciudadania o estatus migratorio calificado. Puede solicitar en linea en gateway.ga.gov, en su oficina local de DFCS, o en un centro de salud participante para Elegibilidad Presuntiva.

es.question: Despues de que termine mi RSM posparto, cuales son mis opciones en Georgia?
es.answer: Cuando finalice su cobertura posparto RSM de 12 meses, tiene varias opciones. La perdida de Medicaid es un evento calificador que activa un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias para el Mercado de Georgia Access; inscribase en georgiaaccess.gov dentro de los 60 dias para un plan del Mercado ACA con creditos fiscales si su ingreso esta entre el 100% y el 400% FPL en 2026. Si su ingreso esta bajo el 100% FPL, solicite Georgia Pathways to Coverage o Medicaid Familiar si tiene hijos menores de 19. Si queda embarazada nuevamente, la elegibilidad RSM se reinicia de inmediato.

stateRules.rule: Right from the Start Medicaid (RSM) covers pregnant women at 220% FPL. Georgia counts a pregnant woman as two or more household members. Postpartum RSM coverage extends 12 months after birth (ARP extension, effective 2023). Georgia has NOT expanded Medicaid for non-pregnant adults under standard ACA expansion.

Georgia Pathways to Coverage provides partial Medicaid expansion for adults who complete 80 hours per month of qualifying work or community engagement activity and have income under 100% FPL. Pregnant women are EXEMPT from the Pathways work requirement.
PeachCare for Kids (CHIP) covers children in households earning up to 247% FPL from birth through age 18. Newborns qualify from the date of birth; apply within 60 days at gateway.ga.gov.

Georgia Presumptive Eligibility (PE) for pregnant women allows qualified entities (FQHCs, county health departments) to grant same-day temporary RSM Medicaid coverage while the full application is reviewed by DFCS.

heading.en: COBRA vs. Georgia RSM Medicaid vs. Georgia Access Marketplace: Which Should You Choose?
heading.es: COBRA vs. Medicaid RSM de Georgia vs. Mercado de Georgia Access: Cual Debe Elegir?

body.en: Georgia RSM Medicaid is the clear first choice for pregnant women who qualify. RSM charges no premiums and no copays for prenatal care and delivery, it has no enrollment deadline, and it accepts applications year-round. The only question is whether your income falls at or below 220% FPL (approximately $47,608 per year for a single pregnant woman counted as a household of two in 2026). COBRA preserves your former employer's plan at 102% of the full premium, typically $400 to $900 per month for an individual in 2026, and makes sense only if you need to maintain a specific high-risk OB specialist whose practice is not contracted with any Georgia Medicaid MCO or Georgia Access Marketplace plan. Georgia Access Marketplace plans cover maternity care as an essential health benefit under the ACA, and premium tax credits reduce costs significantly for incomes between 100% and 400% FPL at georgiaaccess.gov; however, pregnancy alone does not trigger a Special Enrollment Period in Georgia, so a Marketplace option is viable only if you are already enrolled or qualify under another SEP trigger. The decision tree for 2026: apply for RSM Medicaid first at gateway.ga.gov; if income exceeds 220% FPL, compare Georgia Access Marketplace Silver plans with cost-sharing reductions; elect COBRA only as a last resort when your specific provider network cannot be matched by RSM Medicaid MCOs or any Georgia Access plan.
body.es: El Medicaid RSM de Georgia es la primera opcion clara para las mujeres embarazadas que califican. RSM no cobra primas ni copagos por atencion prenatal y parto, no tiene fecha limite de inscripcion y acepta solicitudes todo el ano. La unica pregunta es si sus ingresos son iguales o inferiores al 220% FPL. COBRA mantiene el plan de su antiguo empleador al 102% de la prima completa, tipicamente $400 a $900 por mes para un individuo en 2026, y tiene sentido solo si necesita mantener un especialista de alto riesgo especifico cuya practica no esta contratada con ninguna MCO de Medicaid de Georgia o plan del Mercado de Georgia Access. Los planes del Mercado de Georgia Access cubren la atencion de maternidad como beneficio esencial de salud bajo la ACA.
